notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0003] Read the target module and tests before editing: Start by reading the file to be modified, related models/utilities, and any existing tests for the feature to align signatures and behavior.
  Cat invoice.py, models.py, money.py, and tests/test_average_unit_price.py before writing code. This reveals the exact stub signature, dataclass field names (line.quantity, line.unit_price), and expected return type, enabling a first-attempt pass.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal math: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and models.py first to learn the money policy. Wrap inputs with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round results with round_money so rounding and type conventions match the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0002] Guard division with a zero-total check: For weighted-average or ratio computations, check the denominator before dividing and return the documented fallback (ZERO) when it is zero.
  Compute total_quantity first; if it is falsy, return ZERO immediately. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement and avoids ZeroDivisionError without try/except.
- [rb-0004] Match existing error codes and validation patterns before implementing: Grep the codebase for similar validation (state checks, amount checks) to reuse established BillingError codes and message formats.
  Before writing validation logic, search for existing patterns like `invalid_state` or `negative_amount` in sibling modules. Reusing the same error codes and f-string message formats keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on codes.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool when validating integer types: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(x, int) accepts True/False; explicitly reject bools for integer-only parameters.
  When a parameter must be a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before the range check. Otherwise True would pass as quantity 1 and silently corrupt data.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money inputs through the project's to_money helper: Convert raw unit_price values with the existing to_money/round_money utilities before comparing or storing, rather than assuming Decimal.
  Call `to_money(unit_price)` to coerce inputs, then compare against the module's ZERO constant for negativity. This handles ints, strings, and Decimals uniformly and keeps stored LineItem values consistent with the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Reuse existing timezone-normalization helpers
item.description: When implementing date arithmetic, normalize inputs with the repo's existing UTC helper rather than assuming tz-awareness.
item.content: Before writing datetime logic, grep for helpers like ensure_utc in sibling modules (e.g. subscriptions.current_period) and apply them to all inputs. This keeps behavior consistent with the rest of the codebase and avoids naive/aware comparison errors.

item.title: Compute periodic occurrences with floor division
item.description: For 'first occurrence strictly after t' with fixed period from a start, use (t - start) // period then add one period.
item.content: Compute n = (after - start) // length, then renewal = start + (n+1)*length, with a small while-loop guard to enforce strict inequality. Handle after < start separately by returning start + length, since the start itself is not a renewal.

item.title: Verify edge cases with a quick script after tests pass
item.description: Passing tests isn't enough; probe boundary inputs (exact boundary, before start, just-before boundary) with an ad-hoc script.
item.content: After the test suite passes, run a short inline Python snippet exercising exact-boundary, pre-start, and off-by-one-second cases. This catches strict-vs-inclusive semantics bugs that a single happy-path test misses.
